system.name: SPEX
system.one_liner: a speculative exploration framework that breaks the reward-feedback barrier in tree-of-thought reasoning

content.subject: how SPEX simulates speculative rollouts on a search tree, updating visit counts and values before each real exploration

content.key_idea: A node's fill colour (grey/yellow/green) tracks whether it is explored, the current main-branch choice, or a speculative lookahead candidate, and a dashed box isolates the speculative-simulation frames that run ahead of the confirmed rollout.
content.reading_order: Top-down through Depth-First Search's two example rows in (a), each frame left to right into and out of its dashed speculative-simulation box; then Breadth-First Search's single frame row in (b).

encoding.color_means: grey marks nodes whose rollout is already explored, yellow marks the node currently chosen on the real (main) branch, green marks nodes being speculatively explored ahead of confirmation, and red text flags a value or visit count that just changed
encoding.line_style_means: plain black edges draw the fixed tree shape in every frame; dashed rectangles group the frames that belong to one speculative-simulation lookahead
encoding.state_means: a node's fill colour (grey/yellow/green/white) tells explored, main-branch, speculative, or untouched apart, and is redrawn identically in each frame so only the colours and V/C numbers change
encoding.marker_means: circled numbers 1-7 are persistent node identities, not step order; V and C labels tag each node's value estimate and visit count
encoding.emphasis: red numerals highlight exactly which value or visit count a frame just updated, and the dashed box isolates the lookahead frames from the confirmed rollout on either side
reusable_patterns: a fixed small tree redrawn frame by frame with only node colour and V/C numbers changing, and a dashed box isolating a speculative lookahead sub-sequence between two confirmed frames
weaknesses: node numbering restarts and reuses the same 1-5 labels across the two DFS examples and the BFS panel, so the two examples must be told apart by their captions rather than by node identity
the caption text supplied for panel (b) is cut off mid-sentence, so the exact softmax allocation rule is not fully readable here

evidence: If the selected node is already under speculative expansion, it is skipped.
the speculative budget matches the count of completed nodes
shorter branches finish significantly earlier than the longest ones

summary: Figure 9 walks through SPEX's speculative rollout mechanism on a small search tree, using a shared legend of grey (explored), yellow (main-branch exploring), and green (speculative exploring) nodes annotated with value V and visit count C. In (a) Depth-First Search, two examples show a boxed 'speculative simulation' sub-sequence: starting from a chosen node, SPEX simulates k further iterations ahead of the real choice, incrementing candidate nodes' visit counts (shown in red) frame by frame, before the outer rollout resumes with the newly explored nodes marked speculative (green). In (b) Breadth-First Search, frames show speculative branches expanded onto already-completed nodes (e.g., node 2) while a too-small branch (node 4) is excluded, illustrating how SPEX fills idle slots left by faster-finishing branches with additional speculative expansions instead of waiting.
